correctness.rationale: Proved every greedy complete arch length 3 or 4 and last remainder at most 3 using the binary squarefree length-3 ceiling. For length-four arch abac the next such arch is forced to babc; four consecutive are the forbidden square (abac babc)^2. Partition m arches into disjoint sets of four, obtaining at least floor(m/4) short arches and the exact n upper bound. The length-18 squarefree witness has 4 arches; hence n=19 forces 5. Independent stdlib code verifies the one-to-three-to-four long-arch classification, all 1830 words at length 19 and direct subsequence coverage.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Squarefree words are a proper subset of adjacent-distinct ternary words. No lower bound of positive density can be transferred from the larger language: arbitrarily long two-letter alternating words are adjacent-distinct but not one-universal over three symbols. The published general counting algorithms do not provide this explicit structural result without separate square-avoidance analysis.

value.rationale: This connects two genuinely distinct structures: forbidden contiguous squares and required scattered patterns. The forced alternating transition of complete arches is a reusable local rigidity principle; it sharpens the global guaranteed density from 1/4 to 4/15 and identifies the first nontrivial sharp 5-universality forcing threshold at n=19. Neither a tiny isolated numerical gain nor a computational table alone is the finding. The 4/15 asymptotic coefficient is not advertised as optimal.
